title.zh: 卷423 列傳二百十 宗稷辰 尹耕雲 王拯 穆缉香阿 游百川 沈淮
title.en: Volume 423 Biographies 210: Zong Jichen, Yin Gengyun, Wang Zheng, Mu Jixianga, You Baichuan, Shen Huai
title.raw: 卷423 列傳二百十 宗稷辰 尹耕雲 王拯 穆缉香阿 游百川 沈淮

sentences.zh: =宗稷辰= 宗稷辰，字滌甫，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: =Zong Jichen= Zong Jichen, courtesy name Difu, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Jichen, whose courtesy name was Difu, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光元年舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Daoguang reign he passed the provincial examination, was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his provincial degree in the first year of Daoguang (1821), was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 遷起居注主事，再遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a director in the Office of Daily Annals, and was again transferred to be an assistant department director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Office of Daily Annals, then to assistant department director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he was transferred to be a supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851) he became a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 疏請飭各省實行保甲，略言：「州縣宜久任，時日宜寬假，填寫門牌當詳細核對，董事胥役毋派費累民，酌用丞簿以為襄助，先編巨族以為聯屬，並可申明讀法之典，兼收團練、社倉之益。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting that every province be ordered to put the baojia system into effect, stating in summary: "Prefects and magistrates should serve long terms; deadlines should allow ample time; door placards should be filled in with detailed verification; clerks in charge and runners must not be assigned fees that burden the people; assistant and registrar officials may suitably be employed to assist; great clans should first be registered to form linked groups; and provisions for promulgating the texts on law may also be declared, together gaining the benefits of militia drill and community granaries."
translations.idiomatic: He urged the throne to require every province to enforce the baojia household system, arguing that magistrates should stay in post long enough to see reforms through, that registration deadlines should be realistic, that door placards must be checked carefully, that clerks must not extort the public, that junior officials could help supervise, that leading families should be registered first to anchor neighborhood groups, and that reading the law aloud could reinforce the system while tying in militia drill and community granary benefits.

sentences.zh: 」詔下直省督撫，各就地體察參酌行之。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the governors-general and governors of each province, ordering each to investigate local conditions on the spot and carry out measures with due discretion.
translations.idiomatic: The edict went to every provincial governor to adapt and implement the plan according to local conditions.

sentences.zh: 又疏言通籌出入，宜崇實去偽，舉清查、報效、生息三端；

translations.literal: He also memorialized on coordinating revenue and expenditure, stating that truth should be honored and falsity rejected, and citing three measures: thorough investigation, voluntary contributions, and interest-bearing reserves;
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial on balancing the budget he urged honesty over window-dressing and highlighted three remedies: rigorous audits, voluntary surcharges, and interest-bearing reserve funds.

sentences.zh: 又疏請酌改經徵處，分令州縣戴罪嚴催：並下戶部覈議。

translations.literal: He also memorialized asking that collection points be suitably revised and that prefectures and counties be ordered separately to press collection under penalty of guilt: the matter was also sent down to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed adjusting tax collection districts and ordering each prefecture and county to pursue arrears under threat of disciplinary action; the Ministry of Revenue was instructed to review the plan.

sentences.zh: 五年，聞上將謁陵，未有旨戒行，稷辰疏言：「畿南州縣被水，連歲用兵，民氣甫行休息，籥請展緩一年。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, hearing that the emperor was about to visit the imperial tombs though no edict had yet been issued forbidding travel, Jichen memorialized: "The prefectures and counties south of the capital have suffered flooding; war has continued for years; the people's strength has only just begun to recover— I respectfully ask that the visit be postponed for one year."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng (1855), learning that the emperor planned a tomb visit though no travel ban had been announced, Jichen argued that flood-stricken counties south of the capital had barely recovered from years of war and begged that the journey be deferred a year.

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「每歲謁陵，事同典禮，如果畿輔民力未逮，亦必權衡時勢，暫緩舉行。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "The annual tomb visit is a matter of ritual propriety; if the people's strength in the capital region is insufficient, the times must certainly be weighed and the ceremony temporarily postponed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that the annual tomb visit was a ritual obligation, but that if the capital region could not bear the burden, the court would weigh the circumstances and postpone it.

sentences.zh: 今茲並未降旨何日謁陵，宗稷辰揣度陳奏，徒博敢諫之名而無其實。

translations.literal: At present no edict has even been issued fixing the date of the tomb visit; Zong Jichen guessed and memorialized, merely seeking the reputation of bold remonstrance without the reality.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no date for the visit had even been set; Jichen had merely speculated and spoken up, winning a reputation for bold remonstrance without any real issue at stake.

sentences.zh: 此風不可長！

translations.literal: This practice must not be allowed to spread!
translations.idiomatic: Such posturing must not be encouraged!

sentences.zh: 」下部議處。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the ministries for deliberation on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries were ordered to decide his punishment.

sentences.zh: 尋又奏言：「自粵匪竄據長江，數年以來，文臣武將，能戰者稀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again memorialized: "Since the Cantonese rebels seized positions along the Yangtze, over several years civil and military officials who can fight have been few."
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted another memorial: "Since the Taiping rebels took the Yangtze, few civil or military officials have proved able in the field."

sentences.zh: 如烏蘭泰、塔齊布、江忠源皆難得之將，而多不盡其用，且以死殉。

translations.literal: Men such as Ulang'a, Taqibu, and Jiang Zhongyuan were all generals hard to obtain, yet many were not fully employed and moreover died in service.
translations.idiomatic: Generals as rare as Ulang'a, Taqibu, and Jiang Zhongyuan were often underused and died before their talents were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 如勝保、張亮基、袁甲三皆勇於任事，而亦未盡其用，以罪罷去。

translations.literal: Men such as Sheng Bao, Zhang Liangji, and Yuan Jiasan were all bold in undertaking affairs, yet they too were not fully employed and were dismissed on charges.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao, Zhang Liangji, and Yuan Jiasan were willing to take responsibility, yet they too were sidelined and removed on disciplinary grounds.

sentences.zh: 近日支持兩湖，賴有一二書生，如胡林翼、羅澤南，能以練膽為士卒先。

translations.literal: Recently in holding up the two Hu provinces we have relied on one or two scholars, such as Hu Linyi and Luo Zinan, who could take the lead in drilling courage among the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Hubei have lately been sustained chiefly by a few scholar-officers such as Hu Linyi and Luo Zinan, who drilled their men in courage and led from the front.

sentences.zh: 此二人者，實曾國籓有以開之。

translations.literal: These two men in fact had Zeng Guofan to open the way for them.
translations.idiomatic: In truth Zeng Guofan had paved the way for both of them.

sentences.zh: 此時若開文武兼資一科，誠足濟當時之急，而臣工多不敢薦舉者，一恐其才疏而得過，一恐其遇蹇而罔功。

translations.literal: At this time if a special examination for men combining civil and military talent were opened, it would truly suffice to meet the urgent needs of the day; yet many officials dare not recommend, fearing on the one hand that the candidate's ability may be shallow and they be faulted, and on the other that he may meet adversity and achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: A special recruitment track for men skilled in both civil and military affairs would meet the emergency, yet officials hesitate to recommend anyone—afraid of being blamed if the nominee proves incompetent, or of backing a capable man who still fails through bad luck.

sentences.zh: 處愁眉焚頂之時，守蹈常習故之轍，見有敗衄，動以餉匱為辭。

translations.literal: In a time when brows are knit and heads burn with worry, they cling to the beaten track of routine; whenever defeat occurs, they promptly take shortage of funds as their excuse.
translations.idiomatic: At a moment of national crisis they cling to routine; after every defeat they blame lack of funds.

sentences.zh: 餉固不可不籌，試思用兵乏人，雖斂金百萬，棄如土苴，終歸無用。

translations.literal: Funds certainly cannot go unplanned, but consider: if in employing troops men are lacking, even if a million in gold is levied and cast aside like clods of earth, in the end it is useless.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies must be found, but without commanders a million taels of silver is worthless rubble on the ground.

sentences.zh: 臣聞見隘陋，非能盡識天下之才，所知湖南有左宗棠，通權達變，為疆吏所倚重，若使獨當一面，必不下於林翼、澤南。

translations.literal: Your servant's knowledge is narrow and shallow and cannot encompass all talent under heaven; of those I know, in Hunan there is Zuo Zongtang, versatile and resourceful, relied upon by frontier officials—if he were given independent command of a front, he would certainly be no inferior to Linyi and Zinan.
translations.idiomatic: My own horizon is limited, but in Hunan I know Zuo Zongtang, a flexible strategist provincial governors already trust; given an independent command he would rank with Hu Linyi and Luo Zinan.

sentences.zh: 其屢經論薦，難進易退，肝膽經術，實可取材者，有若湖州之姚承輿。

translations.literal: One who has repeatedly been discussed and recommended, is hard to advance and easy to retire, and in courage and classical learning is truly fit for employment, is Yao Chengyu of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly recommended yet hard to place is Yao Chengyu of Huzhou, whose courage and scholarship make him worth employing.

sentences.zh: 其策議深沉，才識過人者，有若常州之週騰虎、管晏，桂林之唐啟華，皆關心時務，今尚鬱鬱伏處田間。

translations.literal: Those whose policy deliberations are profound and whose talent and insight surpass others include Zhou Tenghu and Guan Yan of Changzhou and Tang Qihua of Guilin—all concerned with current affairs, yet still depressed and living in retirement in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Men of deep strategic insight include Zhou Tenghu and Guan Yan of Changzhou and Tang Qihua of Guilin—all engaged with public affairs, yet still living in obscurity in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 誠能破格招賢，連茹並進，則得一人可以平數州，得數人可以清一路。

translations.literal: If talent were truly recruited by breaking precedent and advancing men in linked groups, then obtaining one man could pacify several prefectures, and obtaining several men could clear an entire route.
translations.idiomatic: If the court broke precedent and brought such men forward in groups, one appointee could pacify several prefectures and a handful could secure an entire war zone.

sentences.zh: 長江雖阻，當不難分道建功，剋日平定。

translations.literal: Though the Yangtze is obstructed, it should not be difficult to achieve merit on separate fronts and pacify the realm on a set day.
translations.idiomatic: Even with the Yangtze blocked, coordinated offensives could still bring a swift end to the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 伏乞皇上命內外臣工各舉所知，無論已仕未仕，果能文武兼資，皆許徵起，必可網羅而盡得之。

translations.literal: I respectfully beg Your Majesty to order civil and military officials within and without to each recommend those they know; whether already in office or not, if they truly combine civil and military qualifications, all may be summoned to service, and talent can surely be gathered in full.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to order every official to recommend men of proven civil and military ability, in or out of office, so that the full pool of talent may be mobilized.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下各督撫，命以宗棠等加考送部引見。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was sent down to each governor-general and governor, ordering that Zongtang and the others undergo additional examination and be sent to the ministries for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was circulated to the provinces with orders to examine Zuo Zongtang and the others and send them to court for audience.

sentences.zh: 宗棠自此膺簡拔，論者謂其知人。

translations.literal: From this Zongtang received imperial selection, and commentators said that Jichen knew men.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang was thus brought into service, and observers credited Jichen with recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 時京師行大錢，商民苦之。

translations.literal: At the time the capital was circulating large coins, and merchants and common people suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: Large-denomination coins were then in circulation in the capital, to the distress of merchants and the public.

sentences.zh: 稷辰上疏請復用制錢，號曰「祖錢」，而大錢改純用鐵鑄，兼行並用。

translations.literal: Jichen memorialized asking that standard copper cash be restored, to be called "ancestral cash," while large coins were to be recast purely in iron and both kinds used together.
translations.idiomatic: Jichen urged restoring standard copper cash under the name "ancestral coins," recasting large coins in iron only, and circulating both side by side.

sentences.zh: 下部議，格不行。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated, but the proposal was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries reviewed the plan but rejected it.

sentences.zh: 又以畿輔水患，疏請急賑，從之。

translations.literal: Because of flooding in the capital region he also memorialized requesting urgent relief, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged emergency relief for flood victims in the capital region, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋授山東運河道，捻匪入境，於濟寧牛頭河濱築戰牆，北岸六千三百丈，南岸八千六百丈，賴以守禦。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed commissioner of the Shandong grain transport route; when Nian bandits entered the province, at Jining on the bank of the Niutou River he built battle walls—six thousand three hundred zhang on the north bank and eight thousand six hundred zhang on the south—and relied on them for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Shandong grain-transport commissioner; when Nian bandits invaded he built fortified walls along the Niutou River at Jining—6,300 zhang on the north bank and 8,600 on the south—which held the line.

sentences.zh: 以功加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the brevet rank of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he received the brevet rank of salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，引疾歸，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Tongzhi reign he cited illness and retired, and soon afterward died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tongzhi (1867) he retired on grounds of illness and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 稷辰父霈正，官湖南零陵知縣，廉無餘貲。

translations.literal: Jichen's father Peizheng served as magistrate of Lingling in Hunan and was incorruptible, leaving no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His father Peizheng had been magistrate of Lingling in Hunan and died leaving nothing beyond an honest official's meager estate.

sentences.zh: 稷辰事母孝。

translations.literal: Jichen was filial in serving his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Jichen was devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 為學宗王守仁、劉宗周。

translations.literal: In learning he took Wang Shouren and Liu Zongzhou as his masters.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he followed Wang Yangming and Liu Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 罷官後，主餘姚龍山書院、山陰蕺山書院。

translations.literal: After leaving office he headed the Longshan Academy in Yuyao and the Jishan Academy in Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he directed the Longshan Academy in Yuyao and the Jishan Academy in Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 官京朝，請祀總兵葛雲飛本籍；

translations.literal: While serving in the capital he requested that Brigadier General Ge Yunfei be enshrined in his native place;
translations.idiomatic: While at court he secured a shrine in Ge Yunfei's home county for the fallen general Ge Yunfei;

sentences.zh: 官山東，請修方孝孺祠，並刻正學集：其振勵風教多類此。

translations.literal: while serving in Shandong he requested repair of the shrine to Fang Xiaoru and the printing of his Correct Learning collection: his efforts to revive custom and instruction were largely of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: and in Shandong he restored Fang Xiaoru's shrine and published his Correct Learning collection—typical of his efforts to uphold moral example.

sentences.zh: =尹耕雲= 尹耕雲，字杏農，江蘇桃源人。

translations.literal: =Yin Gengyun= Yin Gengyun, courtesy name Xingnong, was a native of Taoyuan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Gengyun, whose courtesy name was Xingnong, came from Taoyuan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年進士，授禮部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a director in the Ministry of Rites, and was again promoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirtieth year of Daoguang (1850), entered the Ministry of Rites as a director, and was later promoted to department director.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，粵匪犯畿輔，惠親王綿愉為大將軍，僧格林沁參贊軍務，闢耕雲佐幕府，上書論防務，為文宗所知。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels threatened the capital region; Prince Hui Mianyu was made grand general, Sengge Rinchen assisted in military affairs, and Gengyun was recruited to the staff; he submitted writings on defense and became known to the Wenzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855, when Taiping forces threatened the capital, Prince Hui Mianyu took overall command with Sengge Rinchen as his deputy; Gengyun joined the staff, wrote on frontier defense, and came to the attention of Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 八年，授湖廣道監察御史，署戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed supervising censor for the Huguang circuit and acted as supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng (1858) he became supervising censor for Huguang and acted as supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 時方多事，封章月數上。

translations.literal: The times were troubled, and he submitted sealed memorials several times each month.
translations.idiomatic: In those crisis years he filed several memorials every month.

sentences.zh: 直隸總督訥爾經額坐貽誤封疆罷，復起。

translations.literal: The governor-general of Zhili, Ne'erjing'e, was dismissed for having endangered the frontier, then was reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili governor-general Ne'erjing'e had been dismissed for endangering the frontier, then was brought back to office.

sentences.zh: 耕雲疏言：「訥爾經額之罪，天下共聞共見，未喻其復行起用之故。

translations.literal: Gengyun memorialized: "Ne'erjing'e's offenses are known to all under heaven, seen by all; the reason for his reappointment is not understood."
translations.idiomatic: Gengyun protested: "Ne'erjing'e's failures are notorious, and no one understands why he has been restored."

sentences.zh: 方今江、淮、楚、豫軍務未靖，秉鉞之臣，星羅棋布，所以奮不顧身，必欲滅此朝食者，固由篤於忠義，亦以國家信賞必罰，有以畏服其心。

translations.literal: At present military affairs along the Yangtze, Huai, Chu, and Yu are not yet pacified; commanders bearing axes are spread like stars in the sky or pieces on a board; the reason they throw themselves forward and must destroy the enemy before breakfast is indeed that they are deeply loyal, but also that the state rewards and punishes with certainty, so that their hearts are held in awe.
translations.idiomatic: With fighting still raging along the Yangtze, Huai, Chu, and Henan, field commanders risk everything not only from loyalty but because they trust the throne to reward merit and punish failure.

sentences.zh: 萬一效尤解體，患何可言？

translations.literal: If others follow his example and the army disintegrates, what disaster can be described?
translations.idiomatic: If others follow his example the armies may fall apart—what then?

sentences.zh: 昔宣宗起用琦善，以陳慶鏞之言而罷。

translations.literal: Formerly the Xuanzong Emperor reappointed Qishan, but because of Chen Qingyong's words he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong once reappointed Qishan, only to dismiss him after Chen Qingyong's remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 伏原紹述心傳，收回成命。

translations.literal: I respectfully beg that Your Majesty continue the transmitted intent of the heart and withdraw the completed order.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to honor that precedent and revoke the appointment.

sentences.zh: 」 時粵匪复窺武漢，耕雲疏言：「武漢地踞上游，北窺關陝，南脅湖湘，東撼吳越，西製巴蜀，自古南北用兵，皆出死力爭之。

translations.literal: At that time the Cantonese rebels again cast their eyes on Wuhan; Gengyun memorialized: "Wuhan lies in the upper reaches; to the north it overlooks Guanzhong and Shaanxi, to the south it threatens Hunan and Hubei, to the east it shakes Wu and Yue, to the west it controls Ba and Shu; from antiquity in warfare between north and south all have striven for it with their utmost strength."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels again threatened Wuhan, Gengyun wrote that the city commanded the upper Yangtze, threatened Shaanxi to the north, Hunan and Hubei to the south, the lower Yangtze to the east, and Sichuan to the west—and that north-south wars had always been decided there.

sentences.zh: 今賊窺伺楚北，分擾廣濟、黃岡，逼近省城，撫臣胡林翼兵勇數千，眾寡懸絕，江路綿遠，首尾不能兼顧。

translations.literal: Now the rebels watch northern Chu, divide forces to harass Guangji and Huanggang, and press close to the provincial capital; the governor Hu Linyi has only a few thousand troops, the disparity in numbers is extreme, the river route is long and distant, and he cannot attend to both head and tail.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel columns now probed northern Hubei, raided Guangji and Huanggang, and closed on the provincial capital; Governor Hu Linyi had only a few thousand men on a long river line and could not cover every threat.

sentences.zh: 侍郎曾國籓忠勇樸誠，應請授為欽差大臣，率其所部援湖北，較諸他臣事半功倍。

translations.literal: The vice president of a ministry, Zeng Guofan, is loyal, brave, plain, and sincere; he should be requested to be appointed imperial commissioner, leading his own forces to relieve Hubei—compared with other officials, he would achieve twice the result with half the effort.
translations.idiomatic: Vice President Zeng Guofan is loyal, brave, and steadfast; he should be made imperial commissioner to lead his army to Hubei's aid—no other choice would achieve so much so quickly.

sentences.zh: 」 粵匪陷定遠，耕雲疏言：「定遠失守，粵、捻新合，必謀北竄，恃山東為之屏蔽。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels took Dingyuan, Gengyun memorialized: "With the loss of Dingyuan, the Cantonese and Nian have newly joined; they will certainly plan to flee north, relying on Shandong as their screen."
translations.idiomatic: After Dingyuan fell, Gengyun warned that Taiping and Nian forces had united and would drive north behind Shandong's shield.

sentences.zh: 撫臣崇恩幸其不戕官據城，於賊退後虛報勝仗，內則巧為彌縫，掩一人耳目；

translations.literal: The governor Chong'en was fortunate that they did not kill officials and seize cities; after the rebels withdrew he falsely reported victories; inwardly he cleverly patched matters over, covering one man's eyes and ears;
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chong'en was relieved the rebels had not slaughtered officials or held cities; after they withdrew he filed false victory reports and papered over failures to deceive his superiors;

sentences.zh: 外則恣其朘削，竭萬姓脂膏。

translations.literal: outwardly he indulged in squeezing the people, exhausting the fat and grease of the myriad populace.
translations.idiomatic: while outwardly he extorted the people until their resources were drained dry.

sentences.zh: 惟懇俯念籓籬重地，立予罷斥，簡大員往代。

translations.literal: I only beg that Your Majesty bend to consider this vital frontier region, immediately dismiss him, and select a senior official to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to dismiss him at once and send a senior replacement to this critical frontier post.

sentences.zh: 於洪湖​​多募水師，兼飭傅振邦全軍移駐固鎮、靈壁，冀收皖北，以固山東。

translations.literal: At Hong Lake recruit many river troops, and also order Fu Zhenbang's entire army to move and garrison at Guzhen and Lingbi, hoping to recover northern Anhui and thereby secure Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit more river forces at Hong Lake, move Fu Zhenbang's entire army to Guzhen and Lingbi, recover northern Anhui, and thereby secure Shandong.

sentences.zh: 」及廬州失守，又​​疏言：「昔人建省安慶，與九江、江寧為犄角，控扼長江。

translations.literal: When Luzhou also fell, he again memorialized: "Former men established the provincial seat at Anqing, forming a horn with Jiujiang and Jiangning to control and choke the Yangtze."
translations.idiomatic: After Luzhou fell he argued that the province had been wisely seated at Anqing, forming a triangle with Jiujiang and Nanjing to control the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 上年徙治廬州，已失形勝，茲並廬州亦不能守。

translations.literal: Last year the seat was moved to Luzhou, already losing the strategic advantage; now Luzhou too cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Moving the capital to Luzhou the year before had already sacrificed strategic advantage; now Luzhou itself was lost.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼等自武漢進逼九江，而安徽之賊，或自英、霍走湖北，牽我上游，或自徽、歙擾浙西，窺我腹地。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi and others advanced from Wuhan to press Jiujiang, while the rebels in Anhui either went from Ying and Huo into Hubei, drawing off our upper Yangtze forces, or from Hui and She to harass western Zhejiang, spying on our interior.
translations.idiomatic: While Hu Linyi pressed Jiujiang from Wuhan, Anhui rebels might strike into Hubei from Yingzhou and Huozhou or raid western Zhejiang from Huizhou and Shexian, threatening the empire's heartland.

sentences.zh: 我軍分道救援，罷於奔命。

translations.literal: Our armies divided to rescue on every route and were exhausted from running to and fro.
translations.idiomatic: Our armies were scattered on relief columns and worn out chasing every alarm.

sentences.zh: 賊有四達之路，我無三面之圍，雖日克一城，何益？

translations.literal: The rebels have roads leading in four directions; we have no encirclement on three sides; though we take a city each day, what use is it?
translations.idiomatic: The rebels can move in every direction while we cannot surround them; capturing a city a day accomplishes nothing.

sentences.zh: 撫臣福濟屢挫損威，候補京堂袁甲三素得民心，如以為巡撫，必奮身圖報。

translations.literal: The governor Fuji's repeated defeats have damaged his authority; the expectant metropolitan graduate Yuan Jiasan has long won the people's hearts—if made governor, he will certainly throw himself forward to repay the favor.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fuji had lost prestige through repeated defeats; Yuan Jiasan, though only an expectant official, enjoyed popular trust and would throw himself into service if made governor.

sentences.zh: 」 及國籓進師，疏言：「軍興以來，徵調半天下，糜餉數千萬，卒未能掃穴擒渠，則以屢後時而數失機也。

translations.literal: When Guofan advanced his army, Gengyun memorialized: "Since the raising of armies, levies have been drawn from half the empire and millions in funds consumed, yet in the end the nest was not swept and the ringleader seized—because opportunities were repeatedly missed by arriving late."
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan marched, Gengyun noted that half the empire had been mobilized and millions spent, yet the rebellion endured because commanders repeatedly arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 今曾國籓蓄養精銳，所向克捷。

translations.literal: Now Zeng Guofan has nurtured elite troops and wherever he turns he wins swift victories.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan had now trained an elite force that won wherever it struck.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成、張洛行率悍賊數十萬，齊向潛山、太湖抗拒，眾寡之數，十倍於我，一有疏虞，關係甚重。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng and Zhang Luoxing led several hundred thousand fierce rebels together to resist at Qianshan and Taihu; in numbers they were ten times ours; a single lapse would have grave consequences.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng and Zhang Luoxing massed hundreds of thousands at Qianshan and Taihu—ten times Zeng's strength—and any slip would be catastrophic.

sentences.zh: 此時廬、鳳、六合賊勢必單，請飭袁甲三、張國樑刻期搗其巢穴，逼令反顧，或令間道為楚師聲援，亦足褫其狂魄。

translations.literal: At this time rebel strength at Lu, Feng, and Liuhe must surely be thin; I ask that Yuan Jiasan and Zhang Guoliang be ordered on a fixed date to strike their nests, forcing them to look back, or that they be sent by side routes to support the Chu army in sound—this too would suffice to strip away their mad spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces at Luzhou, Fengyang, and Liuhe were surely weakened; he urged Yuan Jiasan and Zhang Guoliang to strike their bases on schedule or march by side routes to relieve Zeng's Hunan army and break rebel morale.

sentences.zh: 」別疏劾河道總督庚長，請以甲三兼攝；

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he impeached the director-general of waterways Gengchang and asked that Jiasan also hold that post concurrently;
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he impeached waterways director-general Gengchang and proposed that Yuan Jiasan hold the post concurrently;

sentences.zh: 又論雲南迴匪不宜專意主撫；

translations.literal: he also argued that with the Yunnan Hui rebels one should not focus solely on pacification through appeasement;
translations.idiomatic: he also argued against relying solely on appeasement toward the Yunnan Muslim rebels;

sentences.zh: 又陳京師本計，平糶、採買、周恤、蓄積諸事宜並舉；

translations.literal: he also set forth the capital's fundamental plan, presenting together the matters of fair grain sales, procurement, relief, and storage;
translations.idiomatic: he also laid out a comprehensive capital relief program covering fair-price grain sales, procurement, charity relief, and reserves;

sentences.zh: 又言錢法積弊：諸疏多見採納。

translations.literal: he also spoke of accumulated abuses in the currency system: many of these memorials were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: and exposed long-standing abuses in the currency system; many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 英、法合軍犯天津，耕雲專疏者七，會疏者二，力主決戰，上命王大臣集議。

translations.literal: When British and French combined armies attacked Tianjin, Gengyun submitted seven memorials on his own and joined two joint memorials, strongly urging decisive battle; the emperor ordered princes and grand ministers to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Anglo-French forces attacked Tianjin he filed seven individual memorials and co-signed two more, all urging war; the emperor convened the princes and senior ministers to debate.

sentences.zh: 與鄭親王端華等議不合，耕云抗辯痛哭而罷。

translations.literal: His views did not agree with those of Prince Zheng Duanhua and others; Gengyun argued in opposition, wept bitterly, and the meeting adjourned.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Prince Zheng Duanhua and his faction, argued fiercely, wept, and the council broke up.

sentences.zh: 耕云初在禮部，肅順頗重之，乃是為所憎。

translations.literal: Gengyun had earlier been in the Ministry of Rites, where Sushun greatly valued him; for this he came to be hated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyun had once been valued by Sushun in the Ministry of Rites, which now made Sushun his enemy.

sentences.zh: 九年，科場獄起，以科道失糾下吏議，而耕雲以充內監試譴獨重，鐫二級調用。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the examination-hall case arose; censors and remonstrating officials were faulted for failure to investigate and referred to the ministries for punishment, but Gengyun alone received the heavy penalty for having served as examiner for the eunuchs' test, was demoted two grades, and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1859) the examination scandal broke; censors were generally punished for lax oversight, but Gengyun alone bore the brunt for having supervised the eunuchs' examination and was demoted two ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 十年，京師戒嚴，上將幸熱河，耕雲代團防大臣草疏諫阻，復自以書抵肅順，卒不聽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the capital was placed under martial law; the emperor was about to proceed to Rehe; Gengyun drafted a remonstrance on behalf of the capital-defense commissioner to dissuade him, and also personally sent a letter to Sushun, but in the end they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, with the capital under martial law and the emperor preparing to flee to Rehe, Gengyun drafted a remonstrance for the capital-defense commissioner and wrote personally to Sushun, but the court would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 侍郎文祥提督九門，遇耕雲東城，相持哭，因為規畫留守諸事。

translations.literal: The vice president Wen Xiang was put in charge of the Nine Gates; he met Gengyun in the eastern city, they embraced and wept together, and he thereupon planned the affairs of remaining behind to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Vice President Wen Xiang, commanding the Nine Gates, met Gengyun in the eastern city; they wept in each other's arms and planned the defense of the capital left behind.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼疏薦耕雲胸有權略，請起用。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi memorialized recommending Gengyun as having strategy in his breast and asked that he be reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi recommended Gengyun as a strategist and asked that he be recalled to service.

sentences.zh: 會副都御史毛昶熙治河南團練，疏調從軍。

translations.literal: At the same time the vice censor-in-chief Mao Changxi was managing Henan militia training and memorialized to transfer Gengyun to serve in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Mao Changxi, organizing Henan militia, then had Gengyun transferred to his staff.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，率部卒五千，從僧格林沁平金樓寨教匪，又偕提督張曜克張岡捻巢，以道員記名，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he led five thousand troops, followed Sengge Rinchen in pacifying the sectarian rebels at Jinlou Stockade, and together with Brigadier Zhang Yao captured the Nian nest at Zhanggang; he was recorded by name for the rank of circuit intendant and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he led five thousand men with Sengge Rinchen against the Jinlou Stockade sectarians and with Brigadier Zhang Yao stormed a Nian stronghold at Zhanggang; he was marked for circuit-intendant promotion and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 三年，署河陝汝道。

translations.literal: In the third year he acted as intendant of the He-Shaan-Ru circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he served as acting intendant of the He-Shaan-Ru circuit.

sentences.zh: 西征軍購糧陝州，市斛小，責屬縣償其不足，凡數百萬斤，耕雲悉請罷之。

translations.literal: The western expedition army purchased grain at Shaanzhou; the market bushels were small, and subordinate counties were charged to make up the shortfall—altogether several million jin—Gengyun requested that all of this be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The western expedition bought grain at Shaanzhou in undersized measures and forced counties to make up millions of jin in shortages; Gengyun had the practice abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 客軍有不法者，斬以徇。

translations.literal: When guest troops committed unlawful acts, he beheaded them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He executed offending allied troops as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 境多刀匪，請得節制河、陝兵，饋餉以時，兵咸用命。

translations.literal: The territory had many armed bandits; he requested authority to command the armies of Henan and Shaanxi; rations were delivered on time, and the troops all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: With banditry rife he secured command over Henan and Shaanxi troops, paid them on time, and restored discipline.

sentences.zh: 四年，張總愚犯畿輔，耕雲從巡撫李鶴年進軍磁州，建策築長圍斷賊歸路。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhang Zongyu invaded the capital region; Gengyun followed Governor Li Henian in advancing on Cizhou and proposed building a long encirclement to cut off the rebels' line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865, when Zhang Zongyu threatened the capital region, Gengyun marched with Governor Li Henian to Cizhou and proposed a long encirclement to cut the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 兩署糧儲鹽法道，佐治善後事，濬惠濟河，塞河決，敘勞加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Twice he acted as grain-storage and salt-law intendant, assisting in postwar recovery, dredging the Huiji River, blocking river breaches, and for recorded merit received the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He twice acted as grain and salt intendant, helped manage reconstruction, dredged the Huiji River and sealed breaches, and earned the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，補河陝汝道。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he received regular appointment as intendant of the He-Shaan-Ru circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 he received permanent appointment to the He-Shaan-Ru intendant post.

sentences.zh: 河、陝徭役重，亞於常賦，耕雲立定制，嚴稽覈，民困稍甦。

translations.literal: Corvée labor in Henan and Shaanxi was heavy, second only to regular taxes; Gengyun established fixed regulations and enforced strict audit, and the people's hardship was somewhat relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée burdens in Henan and Shaanxi rivaled regular taxes; he standardized levies and audited them strictly, easing popular distress.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，大旱，條上救荒七事，未及行，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu there was great drought; he itemized seven measures for famine relief, but before they could be carried out he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877 a severe drought struck; he submitted seven famine-relief measures but died in office before they could be implemented.

sentences.zh: 耕雲在言路著直聲，出任監司，巡撫張之萬、李鶴年皆倚重之，軍事多所贊畫。

translations.literal: Gengyun won fame for blunt speech on the remonstrance track; when he went out as a surveillance commissioner, governors Zhang Zhiwan and Li Henian all relied on him, and in military affairs he contributed much planning.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyun was known for blunt memorials; as a provincial commissioner he was trusted by governors Zhang Zhiwan and Li Henian and advised on many campaigns.

sentences.zh: 卒後，巡撫李慶翱以災荒被劾，牽及冒領兵餉事，辭連耕雲，後終得白云。

translations.literal: After his death Governor Li Qing'ao was impeached for famine relief failures, which involved the matter of falsely claiming military pay and implicated Gengyun in the charges; in the end he was finally cleared.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Governor Li Qing'ao was impeached over famine relief and false military-pay claims that implicated Gengyun, but Gengyun was eventually cleared.

sentences.zh: =王拯= 王拯，初名錫振，字定甫，廣西馬平人。

translations.literal: =Wang Zheng= Wang Zheng, original name Xizhen, courtesy name Dingfu, was a native of Maping in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zheng, originally named Xizhen and courtesy-named Dingfu, came from Maping in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年進士，授戶部主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue, and served as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1841, entered the Ministry of Revenue as a director, and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 大學士賽尚阿視師廣西，以拯從，拯感時多難，慷慨思有所建白。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a took command in Guangxi and took Zheng with him; Zheng was moved by the many hardships of the times and generously wished to offer proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a took command in Guangxi, Zheng accompanied him, stirred by the crisis to seek some way to serve.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，自郎中累遷大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng reign he rose from department director through successive promotions to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng era he rose from department director to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，降捻宋景詩由陝西還擾直隸、山東，拯奏言：「景詩岡屯磚圩，儼然嵎固，自陝逸回，其黨不過數百。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, the surrendered Nian bandit Song Jingshi returned from Shaanxi to harass Zhili and Shandong. Zheng memorialized, saying: "Song Jingshi holds Gang Village in a fortified brick stockade, standing firm like a cornered beast; having fled back from Shaanxi, his followers number no more than several hundred."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi (1863), Song Jingshi, a Nian leader who had surrendered, slipped back from Shaanxi to raid Zhili and Shandong. In a memorial, Zheng wrote: "Song Jingshi has fortified Gang Village with brick ramparts and holds it like a beast at bay. Since his escape from Shaanxi, his core band has numbered only a few hundred."

sentences.zh: 崇厚等一再養癰，裹脅逾萬。

translations.literal: Chonghou and others repeatedly nurtured the abscess, and through coercion the force exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chonghou and others repeatedly indulged the problem, until coercion swelled his ranks to more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 近复於昌邑、莘、聊城、臨清四州縣，令村莊將所獲麥與佃戶平分，運送岡屯，是其名為降伏，心跡轉益兇悖。

translations.literal: Recently, in the four prefectures and counties of Changyi, Shen, Liaocheng, and Linqing, he again ordered villages to split harvested wheat equally with tenant farmers and transport it to Gang Village; thus though nominally surrendered, his heart and deeds grew ever more vicious and defiant.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in Changyi, Shen, Liaocheng, and Linqing, he ordered villages to divide the wheat harvest with tenant farmers and send the shares to Gang Village. Though he bore the name of a surrendered man, his conduct grew ever more brutal and rebellious.

sentences.zh: 請密敕直隸督臣劉長佑計調來營，暴其罪而誅之。

translations.literal: I request a secret imperial order to Zhili Governor Liu Changyou to devise a plan to summon him to camp, expose his crimes, and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a secret order be sent to Liu Changyou, governor of Zhili, to arrange his summons to camp, expose his crimes, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 若抗違不至，直隸官軍猶能越境進剿。

translations.literal: If he resists and refuses to come, the Zhili government troops can still cross the border to pursue and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: If he defies the order and does not appear, Zhili's regular forces can still cross the border to attack him.

sentences.zh: 景詩既除，如楊蓬嶺、程順書等首惡，皆可駢誅，以除巨憝，以安畿輔。

translations.literal: Once Song Jingshi is eliminated, chief evildoers such as Yang Pengling and Cheng Shunshu can all be executed together, to remove the great scourge and pacify the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Once Song Jingshi is removed, ringleaders such as Yang Pengling and Cheng Shunshu can be executed together, eliminating a major menace and securing the capital region.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，未行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted but not acted upon.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received, but nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 其後景詩卒以叛誅。

translations.literal: Later Song Jingshi was ultimately executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingshi was eventually executed for treason.

sentences.zh: 軍事未定，曾國籓議於廣東籌餉，勞崇光創辦釐金，諸弊叢起。

translations.literal: With military affairs still unsettled, Zeng Guofan proposed raising funds in Guangdong; Lao Chongguang initiated the lijin tax, and numerous abuses sprang up.
translations.idiomatic: While the war was still unresolved, Zeng Guofan proposed raising funds in Guangdong. Lao Chongguang established the lijin levy, and abuses multiplied.

sentences.zh: 拯疏言：「兩粵為肇亂之區，岑溪、容縣，數載皆為賊踞。

translations.literal: Zheng memorialized, saying: "The two Guang provinces are the regions where disorder originated; Cenxi and Rongxian have for years been occupied by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng submitted a memorial stating: "The two Guang provinces were the cradle of rebellion. Cenxi and Rongxian had been held by bandits for years."

sentences.zh: 信宜陳金缸尤為巨憝，群賊相為一氣，滋蔓難圖。

translations.literal: Chen Jingang of Xinyi is especially a great scourge; the bandits act as one force, spreading and difficult to suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingang of Xinyi was an especially formidable enemy, and the bandits operated as one force, spreading in ways hard to uproot.

sentences.zh: 勞崇光舉辦釐金，率令紳商包充墊繳，燃眉剜肉，事何可常？

translations.literal: Lao Chongguang instituted the lijin, generally ordering gentry and merchants to contract for and advance payment — like cutting flesh to put out a fire; how can such a thing be sustained?
translations.idiomatic: In setting up lijin, Lao Chongguang routinely forced gentry and merchants to contract for collections and advance payments — flesh cut away to douse a fire. Such a method cannot long endure.

sentences.zh: 及崇光去任，徵收減少。

translations.literal: When Chongguang left his post, collection decreased.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongguang left office, collections fell off.

sentences.zh: 近乃有釐務委員，或為眾所毆傷，或為民間枷號，雖民情頑獷，而官吏惡劣亦可概見。

translations.literal: Recently lijin commissioners have been beaten by mobs or publicly pilloried by the people; though the populace is obstinate and fierce, the wretchedness of the officials is also plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, lijin agents have been beaten by crowds or paraded in cangues by local people. However unruly the populace may be, the vileness of the officials is plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 以積年久亂之地，有負嵎圜視之賊，當一切利孔、百方搜剔之時，臣竊恐利未十而害已百。

translations.literal: In a land long torn by years of disorder, with bandits crouching defiantly and watching all around, at a time when every source of profit is being scraped from every direction, I fear that before benefit reaches ten parts, harm will have reached a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In a region long ravaged by chaos, with bandits entrenched and watching for opportunity, and every possible revenue stream squeezed dry from every side, I fear that for every ten parts of gain there will be a hundred parts of harm.

sentences.zh: 萬一兩粵复糜爛，更不知何所措手足，豈惟釐金不能辦而已？

translations.literal: Should the two Guang provinces again be devastated, I would not know where to turn; would it be merely that lijin could not be collected?
translations.idiomatic: If the two Guang provinces were devastated again, the Court would scarcely know what to do — and the failure would be far more than an inability to collect lijin.

sentences.zh: 」因薦廣東道員唐啟廕、兩淮運使郭嵩燾、浙江運使成孫詒。

translations.literal: " He therefore recommended Guangdong circuit intendant Tang Qiyin, Liangjiang transport commissioner Guo Songtao, and Zhejiang transport commissioner Cheng Sunyi.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Tang Qiyin, Guangdong circuit intendant; Guo Songtao, Liangjiang transport commissioner; and Cheng Sunyi, Zhejiang transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋用嵩燾督廣東釐金，自拯疏發之也。

translations.literal: Soon Guo Songtao was appointed to supervise Guangdong lijin — stemming from Zheng's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songtao was soon put in charge of Guangdong lijin, a direct result of Zheng's memorial.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷太常寺卿，署左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acted as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongzhi, he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served concurrently as acting left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏論：「總理各國事務大臣侍郎崇綸、恆祺、董恂、薛煥委瑣齷齪，通國皆知，竊恐外邦輕侮，以為中朝卿貳之班，大都不過如若曹等，未免為中朝恥辱。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "The ministers Chonglun, Hengqi, Dong Xun, and Xue Huan of the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs are petty and sordid — the whole country knows it. I fear foreign powers will treat us with contempt, thinking that among the high officials of the Central Court there are mostly only such men as these — which would be a disgrace to the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Chonglun, Hengqi, Dong Xun, and Xue Huan of the Zongli Yamen are petty and corrupt — a fact known throughout the realm. I fear foreign powers will despise us, believing that even the Court's highest ministers are mostly men of that sort — a humiliation to the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 就令人材難得，或於總理衙門位置為宜，上應量為裁抑，或處以散職，或畀以虛銜，庶外邦服我旌別之嚴。

translations.literal: Even if talented men are hard to find, or if some are suited to posts in the Zongli Yamen, Your Majesty should still measure out restraint upon them — assigning them to nominal posts or empty titles — so that foreign states may respect our strict distinctions of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Even if capable men are scarce, or even if some must remain in the Zongli Yamen, Your Majesty should restrain them appropriately — by assigning nominal posts or empty titles — so that foreign states may respect the strict standards by which we distinguish rank.

sentences.zh: 四方聞之，亦釋然於朝廷宥納群倫、羈縻彼族之意。

translations.literal: When the four quarters hear of this, they will also understand the Court's intent to embrace all ranks and bind those peoples in restraint.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire hears of this, it will also understand the Court's purpose in embracing all classes of men while keeping foreign powers under control.

sentences.zh: 」 尋遷通政使，仍署左副都御史。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to Commissioner of the Transmission Office, still acting as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner of the Transmission Office while continuing to serve as acting left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「近日蘇、杭迭克，直、東肅清。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Recently Suzhou and Hangzhou were taken in succession, and Zhili and Shandong were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he reported: "Suzhou and Hangzhou have recently fallen in turn, and Zhili and Shandong have been pacified."

sentences.zh: 臣觀從來將興之業，垂成之功，未有不矢以小心，而始能底定者。

translations.literal: I observe that enterprises about to flourish and achievements near completion have never failed to be pursued with utmost caution before they could be finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that undertakings on the verge of success are never brought to completion except through the most scrupulous caution.

sentences.zh: 金陵賊窟雖計於三四月間可拔，而丹陽與常州犄角，百戰悍賊如李秀成等，麇集死守。

translations.literal: Though the bandit lair at Jinling is estimated to fall within three or four months, Danyang and Changzhou stand in mutual support; battle-hardened bandits such as Li Xiucheng have massed and hold on to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jinling's rebel stronghold may fall within three or four months, Danyang and Changzhou support each other like horns on a beast, and hardened fighters such as Li Xiucheng have gathered there for a fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 杭、嘉既克，餘黨歸併湖州。

translations.literal: With Hangzhou and Jiaxing taken, the remaining bandits have merged at Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hangzhou and Jiaxing were captured, the remaining rebels consolidated at Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 其自皖南竄越江西之賊，蔓延玉山、鉛山、金谿、建昌二三百里，眾號八九萬，並有闌入福建境者。

translations.literal: Bandits fleeing from southern Anhui across Jiangxi have spread over two or three hundred li through Yushan, Qianshan, Jinxi, and Jianchang — their numbers claimed at eighty or ninety thousand — and some have intruded into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels slipping from southern Anhui into Jiangxi have spread across two or three hundred li through Yushan, Qianshan, Jinxi, and Jianchang, with reported numbers of eighty or ninety thousand, and some have crossed into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 又聞李世賢自率巨股由淳安、遂安接踵而至，曾國籓、左宗棠等用兵日久，前此屢陳不亟求功旦夕，同一老謀深計，獨於皖、浙毗境豫作防維之策，則國籓意在徽、寧各飭所部分防，宗棠以為不若並力取廣德扼賊竄路。

translations.literal: It is also heard that Li Shixian personally leads a large force following close behind from Chun'an and Suian. Zeng Guofan and Zuo Zongtang have been at war a long time; they have repeatedly stated they would not rush for immediate results — sharing the same seasoned strategy — yet on defensive measures along the Anhui-Zhejiang border they differ: Guofan intends to have Huizhou and Ningguo each order their forces to garrison separately; Zongtang holds it better to concentrate strength to take Guangde and block the bandits' escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: It is also reported that Li Shixian is leading a large force close behind through Chun'an and Suian. Zeng Guofan and Zuo Zongtang have fought for years and repeatedly urged against seeking quick victory — they share the same long view — yet on defense along the Anhui-Zhejiang border they differ: Guofan would have Huizhou and Ningguo each assign partial garrisons, while Zongtang argued for concentrating forces to seize Guangde and cut the rebels' escape routes.

sentences.zh: 兩議未及定，賊已由皖竄贛。

translations.literal: Before the two proposals could be settled, the bandits had already fled from Anhui into Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before the two plans could be decided, the rebels had already broken from Anhui into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 賊又草竊已久，人數太眾，勢多不能聚殲而弗使一賊他遁。

translations.literal: The bandits have roamed as marauders for so long, their numbers so vast, that it is often impossible to annihilate them in concentration without letting a single bandit escape elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have long lived by plunder, and their numbers are so great that it is often impossible to destroy them in one blow without letting some escape elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 臣則以此賊人多勢劇，一意奔突，前股未痛剿，後股又踵接。

translations.literal: I take it that with so many bandits and such fierce momentum, they rush forward single-mindedly — before the vanguard is harshly suppressed, the rear column follows close behind.
translations.idiomatic: Because these rebels are numerous and their momentum fierce, they press forward relentlessly: before one column is hard struck, another follows on its heels.

sentences.zh: 萬一深入江西腹地，燼餘复熾，又至燎原。

translations.literal: Should they penetrate deep into the heart of Jiangxi, embers might blaze up again and spread to a prairie fire.
translations.idiomatic: If they drive deep into the interior of Jiangxi, smoldering embers may flare up again and burn across the land.

sentences.zh: 且由贛逾閩，可以直走汀、潮，為數年來竄匪熟路。

translations.literal: Moreover, from Jiangxi crossing into Fujian, they can go straight to Tingzhou and Chaozhou — a familiar route for fleeing bandits these past years.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangxi they can cross into Fujian and strike directly toward Tingzhou and Chaozhou — a well-worn path for fleeing rebels in recent years.

sentences.zh: 黃文金由此而來，石達開由此而去，前事可為深警。

translations.literal: Huang Wenjin came by this route; Shi Dakai departed by it — past events serve as a grave warning.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wenjin came this way; Shi Dakai went out the same way. Past events should serve as a stern warning.

sentences.zh: 疊蒙諭旨，曾國籓、左宗棠、李鴻章、沈葆楨及閩、粵各督撫諄諄戒備。

translations.literal: Repeatedly receiving imperial edicts, Zeng Guofan, Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, Shen Baozhen, and the governors-general and governors of Fujian and Guangdong have been earnestly warned to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts have repeatedly charged Zeng Guofan, Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, Shen Baozhen, and the governors of Fujian and Guangdong to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 當此大功將竟，惟當效力一心，互籌戰守，務將分竄諸賊，前截後追，必使所至創夷，日就衰殘零落，不得喙息，以成巨患。

translations.literal: At this moment when the great achievement is near completion, all should serve with one heart, planning attack and defense together, striving to intercept fleeing bandits from the front and pursue from the rear, so that wherever they go they suffer losses, daily growing weak and scattered, unable to catch breath — lest they become a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: At this moment, when the great victory is nearly won, all should act with one purpose, coordinating offense and defense, cutting off fleeing rebels in front and pursuing from behind, so that wherever they go they are battered and daily weakened until they cannot regroup — lest they become a catastrophe anew.

sentences.zh: 臣尤有請者，皖、浙諸軍與賊相持不為不久，所需餉項，國籓、宗棠等各於江、楚等省自為籌畫。

translations.literal: I have a further request: the armies of Anhui and Zhejiang have contended with the bandits for no short time; for needed supplies, Guofan and Zongtang each arrange funding from Jiangsu, Huguang, and other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: I have another concern: the Anhui and Zhejiang armies have fought the rebels for a long time, and Guofan and Zongtang have each raised funds from Jiangsu, Huguang, and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 國籓奏於江省設立總台，以一省捐釐之數，為皖軍十萬養命之源。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized to establish a general bureau in Jiangsu province, using that province's levy donations as the life-source for a hundred thousand Anhui troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan proposed establishing a central bureau in Jiangsu, using that province's levy contributions as the lifeline for a hundred thousand Anhui troops.

sentences.zh: 浙軍固不能分撥，即國籓所部月餉，傳聞亦祗放數成，不得已而籌及廣東釐捐，乃又不能遽辦。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang army naturally cannot share out; even the monthly pay for Guofan's own forces, it is rumored, is issued at only several tenths; compelled by necessity they turned to Guangdong levy donations, yet these too cannot be quickly raised.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang army cannot spare funds; even the monthly pay for Guofan's own troops, it is said, is disbursed at only a fraction. Out of necessity they turned to Guangdong levies, yet those too cannot be raised quickly.

sentences.zh: 夫民之不能見遠而各為其私者，情也。

translations.literal: That the people cannot see far and each pursues private interest — this is human nature.
translations.idiomatic: That the people cannot see far ahead and each pursues his own interest is only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 廣東有之，江西豈獨不然？

translations.literal: Guangdong has this; would Jiangxi alone be different?
translations.idiomatic: If Guangdong behaves thus, can Jiangxi be any different?

sentences.zh: 日前沈葆楨奏請將江西茶稅、牙釐等款歸本省任收，旋用部議允留其半，在國籓等斷不至觖望。

translations.literal: Recently Shen Baozhen memorialized requesting that Jiangxi tea tax, brokerage lijin, and similar revenues be collected by the province itself; the ministry soon approved keeping half; Guofan and others would certainly not feel resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Shen Baozhen asked that Jiangxi's tea tax, brokerage lijin, and similar revenues be retained for collection by the province. The ministry approved keeping half, and Guofan and the others would surely not take offense.

sentences.zh: 惟軍前將卒，當枕戈喋血切望成功之時，忽聞軍餉來源將減，眾心或生疑懼，何以得飽騰而資鼓舞？

translations.literal: But the officers and soldiers at the front, when lying on their weapons and shedding blood, eagerly hoping for success, suddenly hear that army pay sources will be reduced — hearts may fill with doubt and fear; how can they be fed and inspired to high morale?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the men at the front, sleeping on their arms and shedding blood in eager hope of victory, may suddenly hear that their pay is to be cut. Doubt and fear may spread through the ranks — how then can they be fed, roused, and kept fighting?

sentences.zh: 擬請飭贛、皖、楚、粵各疆臣，值此事機至緊，無論如何變通為難，總當殫竭血誠，同心共濟。

translations.literal: I propose ordering the frontier officials of Jiangxi, Anhui, Huguang, and Guangdong: at this critical juncture, however difficult to adjust matters, they must exhaust utmost sincerity and aid one another with one heart.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the governors of Jiangxi, Anhui, Huguang, and Guangdong be ordered that, at this critical moment, however hard it may be to rearrange affairs, they must give their utmost and act in full concert.

sentences.zh: 甘肅回氛未戢，中州餘捻尚存，汝南陳大喜等竄逸湖北，自隨、棗逼襄、樊；

translations.literal: Muslim unrest in Gansu is not yet quelled; remnant Nian bandits remain in the Central Plains; Chen Daxi of Runan and others have fled into Hubei, pressing on Xiangyang and Fan from Suizhou and Zaoyang;
translations.idiomatic: Muslim rebellion in Gansu is not yet subdued; remnant Nian bands still roam the Central Plains; Chen Daxi of Runan and others have fled into Hubei, advancing from Suizhou and Zaoyang toward Xiangyang and Fan;

sentences.zh: 張總愚自南台山中出竄內、淅，時虞合併；

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu has emerged from the Nantai Mountains into Henan and Shaanxi — there is constant fear they may merge;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyu has broken out of the Nantai Mountains into Henan and Shaanxi, and there is constant fear that these forces may join together;

sentences.zh: 漢中之賊，全竄寧、陝、商州一路，聞將會齊襄、樊回援金陵，誠亦未可輕忽。

translations.literal: Bandits from Hanzhong have all fled along the Ningqiang, Shaanxi, and Shangzhou route; it is heard they will assemble at Xiangyang and Fan to reinforce Jinling — this truly must not be lightly ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Hanzhong have all fled along the route through Ningqiang, southern Shaanxi, and Shangzhou, and it is reported they will gather at Xiangyang and Fan to reinforce Jinling — a threat that must not be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 目前陝省軍務，政出多門，李雲麟追賊商於，忽卷旆而西，其在興安，未能遏賊竄逸，其在漢陰，遇賊避匿，縱勇淫掠，宜量加裁抑。

translations.literal: Currently Shaanxi military affairs suffer divided authority; Li Yunlin pursued bandits at Shangluo, then suddenly withdrew west; at Xing'an he failed to block bandit flight; at Hanyin he avoided bandits and let his troops plunder wantonly — he should be restrained to some degree.
translations.idiomatic: At present Shaanxi's military affairs are divided among too many hands. Li Yunlin pursued rebels at Shangluo, then suddenly marched west. At Xing'an he failed to stop their escape; at Hanyin he shunned battle and allowed his men to loot at will. He should be checked.

sentences.zh: 劉蓉素嘗學問，懷負非常，漢中之賊，本所專辦，而竄擾四出，尤當誓志盪除，方為不負。

translations.literal: Liu Rong has always been a man of learning with extraordinary capacity; the Hanzhong bandits were originally his sole charge, yet they spread disturbances everywhere — he should all the more resolve to exterminate them, or else he fails his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong is a scholar of real ability, and the Hanzhong rebels were originally his responsibility alone. Yet they have broken out in every direction, and he above all should vow to destroy them — or fail in his charge.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿聲望最優，眾口爭傳為第一名將，乃近日聲望漸損，宜申聖諭訓飭。

translations.literal: Duolong'a enjoyed the finest reputation; all mouths proclaimed him the foremost general — yet recently his standing has gradually waned; an imperial instruction of admonition should be issued.
translations.idiomatic: Duolong'a once enjoyed the highest reputation and was widely hailed as the empire's foremost general, yet lately his standing has declined. An imperial admonition should be sent to him.

sentences.zh: 雷正綰所向克捷，諒足當一面之寄，顧全甘官吏，未有一二正人支持其間。

translations.literal: Lei Zhenguan has met with success wherever sent — surely sufficient to entrust with an independent command; yet among Gansu officials there are hardly one or two upright men to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Zhenguan has won victories wherever he has been sent and is surely fit to hold an independent command, yet among Gansu's officials there are scarcely one or two upright men to support him.

sentences.zh: 現聞蘭州與慶陽隔絕，恩麟權督印，不過使令便闢之材，識見陋劣；

translations.literal: It is now heard that Lanzhou is cut off from Qingyang; Enlin holds the governor's seal in acting capacity — but he is merely talent for issuing convenient orders, his vision mean and inferior;
translations.idiomatic: It is now reported that Lanzhou is cut off from Qingyang. Enlin holds the governor's seal in an acting capacity, but he is no more than a man skilled at convenient orders, narrow and inferior in judgment;

sentences.zh: 熙麟坐守慶陽、寧夏一區，又為慶昀種種紕繆所誤。

translations.literal: Xilin sits guarding the Qingyang and Ningxia region, yet is led astray by Qingyun's various blunders.
translations.idiomatic: Xilin holds Qingyang and Ningxia, yet is misled by Qingyun's repeated errors.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為亟宜遴簡公正有為之大臣，鎮撫整飭。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that upright and capable ministers should be quickly selected to pacify and reorganize the region.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit that upright and capable ministers should be chosen at once to restore order there.

sentences.zh: 今之天下，何易遽言率土奠安，而南北軍務漸定，西事再能就緒，亦即為大致之澄清。

translations.literal: Today's empire — how easily can one speak of peace throughout the land? Yet as northern and southern military affairs gradually settle, if western affairs can again be brought to order, that will also mean general clarification.
translations.idiomatic: In the empire today, one cannot lightly speak of universal peace. Yet as military affairs in north and south gradually settle, if the western campaigns can also be brought under control, that will mark a broad restoration of order.

sentences.zh: 朝廷者天下之本，宮府清明嚴肅，與疆場奮迅振拔之氣，相感而自通。

translations.literal: The Court is the root of the empire; when the palace and administration are clear and stern, and the spirit of vigorous advance on the battlefield — these resonate and naturally connect.
translations.idiomatic: The Court is the root of the realm. When the palace and government are clear and disciplined, that spirit resonates with the vigor of the battlefield and the two reinforce each other.

sentences.zh: 天下大勢日轉，而亦正多難鉅之事，或遽以為時局清明，事機暢遂，若已治已安者然。

translations.literal: The great trend of the empire turns daily, yet many difficult and weighty matters remain; some may hastily think the situation clear, affairs smoothly proceeding, as if already governed and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's great tide turns day by day, yet grave difficulties remain. Some may too quickly assume that the times are clear, affairs smooth, and the realm already governed and secure.

sentences.zh: 人情大抵喜新狃常，畏難而務獲，獨有當幾至誠君子，為能深察而切戒之。

translations.literal: Human nature generally delights in the new and clings to habit, fears difficulty and seeks gain — only the sincere gentleman who meets the moment can deeply discern and earnestly warn against this.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature tends to delight in novelty, cling to routine, fear hardship, and chase easy gain. Only the truly sincere man who grasps the moment can see this clearly and warn against it.

sentences.zh: 昔諸葛亮為三代下一人，史獨稱之以謹慎。

translations.literal: Of old Zhuge Liang was deemed the one man beneath the Three Dynasties — history alone praises him for cautiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Of old, Zhuge Liang was called the greatest man since the Three Dynasties, yet history praises him above all for caution.

sentences.zh: 硃子進戒宋孝宗曰：​​'使宴安酖毒之害，日滋而日長；

translations.literal: Zhu Xi admonished Emperor Xiaozong of Song, saying: 'Let the harm of feasting in ease and drinking poison daily grow and daily lengthen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi warned Emperor Xiaozong of Song: "Let the poison of complacent ease daily grow stronger,

sentences.zh: 將臥薪嘗膽之志，日遠而日忘。

translations.literal: the resolve to sleep on brushwood and taste gall daily recede and daily be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: and the resolve to sleep on brushwood and taste gall daily fade and be forgotten."

sentences.zh: '臣不勝私憂過計，冒昧瀝陳。

translations.literal: ' Unable to restrain my private anxiety and perhaps excessive concern, I venture to pour forth these thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to contain my private anxiety, perhaps overstated, I venture to lay these thoughts before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: " The memorial was received; acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and noted.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to retire; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire and died.

sentences.zh: =穆緝香阿= 穆緝香阿，字居南，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: =Mu Jixiang'a= Mu Jixiang'a, styled Junan, a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Jixiang'a, courtesy name Junan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 由工部主事再遷郎中。

translations.literal: From a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works he was promoted again to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from principal clerk in the Ministry of Works to director.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，授山東道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, he was appointed supervising censor of the Shandong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongzhi (1865), he was appointed supervising censor for the Shandong circuit.

sentences.zh: 疏請慎擇宦寺，略言：「皇上沖齡御極，聖學日新，知識日開，左右侍從之輩，宜豫加慎選，勿使將來蠱惑聖聰。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting careful selection of eunuchs, stating in brief: "The Emperor ascended the throne at a tender age; his sacred learning grows daily, his knowledge daily expands — those who attend him at his side should be carefully chosen in advance, lest they in future bewitch and delude the imperial mind.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial urging careful selection of eunuchs, writing in part: "The Emperor came to the throne at a tender age. His sacred learning and understanding deepen daily. Those who attend him should be chosen with the greatest care, lest in time they beguile and corrupt his judgment."

sentences.zh: 溯自漢末及前明，朝政之失，半由宦寺。

translations.literal: Looking back from the end of Han through the former Ming, half the failures of court governance stemmed from eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back from the late Han through the former Ming, half the failures of court governance arose from eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 蓋宦寺出身之始，每以小忠小信，便捷逢迎，無非售其固寵邀恩之計。

translations.literal: For at the outset of a eunuch's rise, with petty loyalty and petty faithfulness, quick to please and fawn — nothing but schemes to secure favor and seek grace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of their careers, eunuchs win favor through small acts of loyalty and quick compliance — all of it designed to secure patronage and reward.

sentences.zh: 及黨與已成，則驕肆專橫，而箝制其上，雖英明之主，竟有百計不能除之者。

translations.literal: Once their faction is formed, they grow arrogant and domineering, controlling those above; even enlightened sovereigns have at last found them irremovable by every stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Once their faction is formed, they grow arrogant and overbearing, constraining their superiors; even wise rulers have found them impossible to remove by any means.

sentences.zh: 當時臣民，切齒痛恨，終歸無可如何。

translations.literal: Officials and people of the time gnashed teeth in hatred — yet ultimately could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and common people alike hated them bitterly, yet in the end could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 我朝列聖相承，遠邁前代，不但不准此輩干預政事，雖應對進退間亦不假以辭色，使無由讒諂面諛，浸潤膚受。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's successive sages, surpassing former ages, not only forbade these people from interfering in state affairs — even in conversation and demeanor they were not granted pleasant words, giving no opening for slander, flattery to the face, or gradual permeation.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's successive sage emperors, surpassing earlier ages, not only barred eunuchs from affairs of state but also refused them even the courtesy of pleasant conversation, leaving no opening for slander, flattery, or slow corruption.

sentences.zh: 是以二百餘年，從不為患。

translations.literal: Thus for over two hundred years they never became a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two hundred years, they therefore never became a menace.

sentences.zh: 雖然如此嚴防，尚有防不勝防之慮。

translations.literal: Though guarded so strictly, there remains concern that guard cannot match every threat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even with such strict precautions, there is fear that vigilance may not suffice.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶癸酉之變，猶有通賊者，是此輩反覆已有明徵也。

translations.literal: In the Guiyou incident of the Jiaqing era, there were still those who colluded with bandits — clear proof of this people's treachery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guiyou uprising of the Jiaqing era, eunuchs were still found colluding with rebels — clear proof of their unreliability.

sentences.zh: 今皇太后垂簾聽政，洞悉其弊，杜漸防微，有鑑於前，不使宵小蒙蔽。

translations.literal: Now the Empress Dowager holds court from behind the curtain, penetrating their evil, stopping gradual decay and guarding against the subtle — with lessons from the past, not letting petty schemers obscure truth.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Empress Dowager reigns from behind the curtain, fully aware of these evils, stopping trouble at its root and taking warning from the past, so that petty schemers cannot obscure her judgment.

sentences.zh: 所以知人善任，朝政肅清。

translations.literal: Hence knowing men and assigning them well; court governance is clear and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Hence she knows men and uses them well, and court governance is clear and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 即數年後皇上親政，亦斷不致寵任此輩，貽誤事機，何待臣下鰓鰓過慮？

translations.literal: Even when in a few years the Emperor personally governs, he will surely not favor and employ these people to the ruin of affairs — why need subordinates fret with anxious foreboding?
translations.idiomatic: Even when the Emperor assumes personal rule in a few years, he will surely not indulge such men to the ruin of state affairs. Why should a subject worry overmuch?

sentences.zh: 然獻曝之忱，有不能已者。

translations.literal: Yet the sincerity of one who offers sun-drying cannot be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the loyalty of one who would offer even his small service cannot be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，正聖學擴充之際，雖臣工皆能盡心輔佐，而宦寺尤宜加意斟酌。

translations.literal: At this time, when sacred learning is expanding — though all ministers can give full devotion in assistance, eunuchs especially warrant deliberate consideration.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, when the Emperor's sacred learning is expanding, all ministers may serve with full devotion, but eunuchs above all require deliberate scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宦寺之設，無非效奔走、供指使而已，萬不可使年輕敏捷之人，常侍左右。

translations.literal: I hold that eunuchs are established for nothing but running errands and taking orders — young and quick-witted men must never constantly attend at the side.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that eunuchs exist only to run errands and obey commands. Young, quick-witted men must never be kept constantly at the Emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 請皇太后選忠正老成者為我皇上朝夕侍從，庶將來親政，必不致受其欺矇蠱惑，而無疆之聖德，基於此矣！

translations.literal: I request the Empress Dowager select men loyal, upright, and mature to attend Our Emperor morning and evening — then when he later governs personally, he will surely not be deceived or bewitched by them, and the boundless sacred virtue will have its foundation here!
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Empress Dowager choose loyal, upright, and mature men to attend the Emperor day and night, so that when he later rules in person he will not be deceived or led astray, and his boundless virtue will rest on this foundation.

sentences.zh: 」 五年，疏論大學士曾國籓督師討捻，日久無功，請量加譴責。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he memorialized criticizing Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan for supervising troops against the Nian for long without success, requesting measured punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tongzhi, he memorialized that Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan, having long commanded the campaign against the Nian without success, should be censured.

sentences.zh: 上以國籓迭疏引咎，特命回任專辦餉糈，雖未蕆全功，非貽誤軍情者可比，斥所奏過當，置不議。

translations.literal: The Emperor, noting Guofan had repeatedly memorialized accepting blame and was specially ordered back to his post to handle provisions alone — though full success was not achieved, this was not comparable to one who botched military affairs — rejected the memorial as excessive and set it aside without deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor noted that Guofan had repeatedly accepted blame and had been specially ordered back to his post to manage supplies; though he had not achieved full victory, this was not the same as dereliction in the field. He dismissed the memorial as excessive and took no action.

sentences.zh: 出為山西蒲州知府，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred out to serve as prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi and soon died.

sentences.zh: 穆緝香阿通知國故，家藏邸報，自國初以來幾備。

translations.literal: Mu Jixiang'a was well versed in national affairs; his household collection of gazettes was nearly complete from the founding of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Jixiang'a was thoroughly versed in state affairs, and his family's collection of court gazettes was nearly complete from the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: =遊百川= 遊百川，字彙東，山東濱州人。

translations.literal: =You Baichuan= You Baichuan, styled Huidong, a native of Binzhou, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: You Baichuan, courtesy name Huidong, came from Binzhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同治元年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the first year of Tongzhi; selected Hanlin bachelor; appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Tongzhi (1862), was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷御史，巡西城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, transferred to censor; inspected the West City.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tongzhi, he was made a censor and assigned to inspect the West City.

sentences.zh: 宗室寬和等所行多不法，奏劾懲治，一時貴近斂跡。

translations.literal: The imperial clansmen Kuanhe and others acted largely unlawfully; he memorialized to impeach and punish them — for a time the noble and intimate restrained their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Kuanhe and others had acted lawlessly in many ways. Baichuan memorialized for their impeachment and punishment, and for a time the privileged at court checked their behavior.

sentences.zh: 七年，捻匪自山東竄直隸，百川奏請飭統兵大臣迅速剿辦，又請嚴禁各省栽種罌粟，上皆採納。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Nian bandits fled from Shandong into Zhili; Baichuan memorialized requesting the commanding generals be ordered to suppress them swiftly, and also requested strict prohibition of opium cultivation in all provinces — the Emperor adopted both.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Nian rebels fled from Shandong into Zhili. Baichuan asked that commanding generals be ordered to suppress them swiftly and also urged a strict ban on opium cultivation in every province. The Emperor accepted both proposals.

sentences.zh: 疏論內外官署胥吏積弊，詔通飭嚴禁。

translations.literal: He memorialized on accumulated abuses of clerks in inner and outer yamens; an edict was issued universally ordering strict prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the longstanding abuses of yamen clerks throughout the central and provincial administrations, and an edict was issued ordering strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 復言：「除吏弊在肅官方，尤在揚士氣。

translations.literal: He further stated: "Eliminating clerk abuses lies in purifying official ranks, and especially in raising the spirit of the scholar-gentry.
translations.idiomatic: He further wrote: "To eliminate clerk abuses, one must first cleanse official ranks, and above all revive the morale of the scholar-gentry."

sentences.zh: 請飭部院堂官於每司中擇賢俊數員，付以事權，專其責任。
